t:
In doubt, Hirkalla decided to have a straight talk. She gathered herself, and went to the throne of Darkness to dispel her fears. At that time, Hinanna took interest in another mortal, and the God of Darkness was left alone.

They had a long conversations. Hirkalla gave him her doubts, and Nihaz answered them. Few people knew what they were talking about but Hinanna returned from her journey and witnessed the end of the talk.

The younger sister learned that Nihaz wanted to overthrow me, All-Mother, and Father Time. He didn't think much of our concept of the world. He mocked the idea of the circle and the renewal of worlds. Nihaz believed that the gods should make mortals our equals, teach them the laws of creation and eternal life.

Hinanna rushed to our divine throne straight away to warn us of the betrayal. I got furious and ordered to bring Hirkalla before my eyes.
This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.
r155884.n: This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.

t:
She was brought to the trial, and accused of being insubordinate. She silently took her sentence and was off to the exile. Since that day, Nihaz was persona non grata in Eidos. Unfortunately, by that time many of the gods were on his side. The creators that didn't want the destruction of their worlds listened to him. This rebel was loved not only by those who belonged to the Darkness but also Chaos and Death. Even gods of elements joined his riot.

I didn't expect him to turn to mortals, helping them fight monsters and improving their lives. His name was praised for giving knowledge and teaching crafts. Nihaz's gifts were poisonous but he gave them generously to his followers. Mortals, who sought immortality and divinity, raised a riot.

Anxiously we have watched from our thrones the growing numbers of Nihaz's army. There was still time until another cycle of destruction and rebirth, but this war couldn't wait. It came to us.
This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.
r155893.n: This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.

t:
Hirkalla, our beloved daughter, then joined Nihaz. With all her heart, she accepted his teaching about the freedom of choice, the breaking of the great circle, and giving the mortals freedom to become gods.

Our worlds were thrown in a long war. Nihaz and the other gods fought against me and Father Time. Sarn, the God of Light, was one of his main enemies at this war.

Nihaz's efforts have given fruit. Gods died one after another. The most terrible thing happened when Nihaz and the others dealt the fatal blow to Father Time. They got him near the World of Destruction, where he engaged in a battle with the Darkness. Only God can kill a God. Nihaz inflicted a fatal blow to Father Time, already wounded, and took away his power. Since then, he became more than the God of Darkness, but hasn't reached what he was looking for.
This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.
r155900.n: This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.

t:
We were wondering what he really wanted. Sarn suggested that his true goal was to raise his own power. He destroyed many gods, including his former allies, Gods of Death and Chaos, and took their power.

Worried by what happened to my husband, I avoided any battles. Eden, the world of Life, became my shelter. The story was simple. I knew that my daughter Hinanna would gain enough experience and wisdom, so eventually she was to become the owner of the divine garden. The Garden of Eden was hidden from Nihaz. Everyone was safe. The war was continued by Sarn, Nihaz's complete opposite. He successfully destroyed legions of darkness, marching through our worlds.

But even a great warrior can fall prey to betrayal. There was a traitor in our ranks. To my surprise, it was Hinanna. Jealous of her sister and her glory with Nihaz, she decided to switch to the stronger side. Hinanna lured Sarn into a trap. After fighting Nihaz, the God of Light was captured.
This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.
r155907.n: This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.

t:
Hinanna strove to be equal to her elder sister. She strove to outperform her. At that time Hirkalla already possessed the power of Darkness and ruled the Death world. Jealous of her sister's might, Hinanna wanted to seize what she posessed.

She gathered secret forces, wore her best clothes and jewelry, and embarked on the journey. She approached the colossal gates of the underground world, awoke the guardian by a loud banging, and fiercely demanded that he let her in.

One cannot enter the Death world and disobey the laws. Hinanna had to give all her clothes and jewels along with all her powers to pass the gates of Ganzir. And she fell under the power of the Death world, ruled by her sister. The young goddess never expected this. She became dead while being alive, and condemned herself to a worse fate.

I knew not what became of Sarn. I knew not of the fate of the younger daughter. Although I felt sorry for the gullible Hinanna that fell victim to her own stupidity, there was a much worse threat hanging over our worlds. The Architect came from far-away world. The heartless Order, where mind and will were one. Nihaz and I had to fight the invader.

I came out of my shelter every once in a while. Having destroyed an emissary of the new enemy, I felt that my lost daughter and a forgotten friend were once again close. When the ship of the missionary of the Order was torn to pieces by my Great Trees, he fell like a ball of fire upon the lifeless world. I gazed upon the empty ground and saw only vile dragons, loyal to Nihaz. I realized that they would summon their King, and left this world. I returned to Eden but never gave up my attempts at finding my lost daughter.

What is mortal's eternity to me? Only an instant. It's been five thousand years. My heart is still yearning.
This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.
r155914.n: This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.

t: I've been watching you, listening to your talks, seeing your deeds. Trust me, I know enough. Most of what you deem important is, in fact, minor. All in due time. Sooner or later, you will understand.

t:
Oh. This is terrible.

But Waterlily does not need to worry... Life is stronger than any sickness. Over the eons of my existence, I have seen so much. Believe me - life always finds a way. Any trials just make it more tenacious. This too will pass like so many other things.

As for Darkness... do not be afraid. Insolent children. I have those, too, unfortunately. Children rebel against their parents, unaware that we do what is best for them.

Only a god can challenge a god, only an immortal can resist an immortal. The fate of mortals is bitter, and every hero is looking for ways to escape their fate. But can they?

I'm starting to understand what my daughter wanted from you. Well, you helped me, and I see no reason to refuse your request.

You learned my lessons, so I didn't doubt your decision. I see this Expedition does not represent everyone who lives in your world. You, Eurial, and Skulnar can stay in my domain.

However, I see the threat coming from Catherina and Felix. They can't win, but they can do enough damage.

You will have to banish them, just as you banished Hirkalla. Help my Children, and they will give you everything my world has to offer.

t: To come with me. All-Mother wants me to take you to the Great Tree. We will talk there. It is not the time for words. It is time to go. Let's not waste it. Do the right thing. All-Mother awaits.
r156051.n: What do you want from me?

t: All-Mother wanted me to find you. She's been talking with you through her creatures, but you didn't hear. Now that we've learned your language, we can talk. Others didn't understand it, no matter how hard they tried. It is hard to fill a cup which is already full. But yours is empty.

We are children of All-Mother, living in the blessed land of Eden. Apparently, you are Children of Sarn. I see it in you. It's amazing! Sarn has long been considered lost. I also see darkness. What a weird mixture...

Who hath the Word to speak, let him speak!

All we do is defend ourselves. Do you wish to speak?
r156054.n: Who hath the Word to speak, let him speak! All we do is defend…

t: Here. Try not to break or lose it.
I'll give you a holographic transmitter. I want you to call me as often as you can and report your latest findings.
r156058.n: How do I get in touch with you?

t:
Get the locals to trust you. Learn who they are, what the want, what their priorities in life are... come up with a way to manipulate them into doing our thing. First of all, we need the ambrosia.

If you come across a goddess, try to reason with her. Nihaz is our common enemy, after all.

If you find something interesting, report to me immediately. Oh yes, and try to find Herbert, Elena, and the others from the base. If they're alive, of course.
r156059.n: What do I need to do?

t:
The locals don't look like weasels. I'm sure they can be trusted.

If it gets violent, don't worry. You'll get a huge monument on the Upper City's central square.

Take your friends and go there. In the meantime, I'll finish what Herbert and Elena started. I suspect that they were on the verge of a great discovery.

February 1, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's notes.

An interesting discovery - we managed to find reduced defense elements on plants around the base.  It seems that some time (probably quite significant) ago, these plants already faced some kind of threat, and after repelling it, they completely lost their properties over several generations.

This needs to be verified. I have a suspicion that the forest around us, for the most part, just wants us to "leave" and not "die in terrible agony." Related to this is the spread of an unusually allergenic pollen that caused massive hay sickness among Penelope employees.

Our next task is to collect new samples during the active spore dispersal phase.
r156075.n: Read page three of the report on Eden flora

t:
January 15, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's notes.

I was able to trace certain successive changes. It seems that local plants develop a certain specialization fairly quickly. Completely different ways of fighting against the Mechanoids, Humans, Aoidoi, Arisen. In the first case, plants develop corrosive properties that attack metals. In the second case, intense biogenic erosion occurs. In the third case, the development of toxicity. In the fourth - accelerated putrefaction.

It seems that the plants around the Penelope have also begun to react to our presence, but fortunately, it's noticeably weaker.
r156076.n: Read the second page of the report on the flora of Eden

t:
January 9, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's notes.

We started researching the local flora. I compared the samples collected at the main base and here. The difference is visible to the naked eye. It seems that the flora at the Gates very quickly acquired the properties necessary for defense and even offense. It is quite curious that the plants seem to interact with each other, as if trying to work out a "single tactic" against us.
r156077.n: Read the first page of the report on Eden flora

t: These are notes from the first report
r156078.n: These are notes from the first report

t:
February 5, 1022. Elena Zimina's Notes.

Important observation: Over the past month, there has been an increase in local animal activity around the Penelope. It seems that the ecosystem is being restructured - the changes are similar to those that occurred near the Bare Ground.

I think there is a center where local animals and plants get the impulse to change their behavior. Hence the conclusion: there's some kind of intelligence out there that is set against us.

We need to take measures to reduce the number of animals around the Penelope, otherwise soon we'll be overrun.
r156085.n: Read the third page of the report on Eden fauna

t:
January 25, 1022. Elena Zimina's Notes.

Incredible! I was able to obtain extremely valuable information. Animals and birds are fundamentally different in their behavior at a distance from the base. They behave more peacefully, almost without interacting with each other. At the same time, near the base they change their way of life - they breed many times more intensively, predators barely touch herbivores, and they all try to get inside the perimeter.
r156086.n: Read the second page of the report on Eden fauna

t:
January 5, 1022. Elena Zimina's Notes.

I want to try and confirm or refute the theory that the animals began to react more aggressively to our presence as soon as we began to extract the Ambrosia more actively. I will go further into the forest to see how animals behave in their usual environment.
r156087.n: Read the first page of the report on Eden fauna

r156088.n: These are notes from the second report

t:
February 13, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's and Elena Zimina's notes.

Amazing discovery! It seems that we managed to find the source of signals that animals and plants are exchanging - it's the roots. The roots of the Great Tree which is the heart of this forest. The roots densely permeate the soil and therefore can easily bind different types of creatures together. Local animals have special receptors on their feet that can read information from sprouts that come to the surface.

We managed to find special nodes, which are like centers where signals from the surrounding forest are collected. Each of these nodes is protected by special thorns that attack from the ground. They are like some kind of brains that coordinate the attacks of the thorns.

According to our observations, every day the thorns become harder and sharper. New samples are required to compare and confirm the hypothesis.
r156111.n: Read page three of the report on defense mutations

t:
January 31, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's and Elena Zimina's notes.

Our observations confirm the following: normally the animals and flora of Eden do not differ from their counterparts from Sarnaut (except here all animals have plant features in their structure, which is a consequence of their completely different origin). However, in a stressful situation - such as the massive deforestation we just carried out, the entire population of organisms undergoes a complete restructuring, and begins to work in a much greater symbiosis, becoming like an army.

The issue of transmitting a signal that allows them to coordinate their actions remains open. At first we thought that telepathy was taking place here, but our mystic on duty, Yolanda, claims these animals and plants do not transmit any thoughts.
r156112.n: Read the second page of the report on defense mutations

t:
January 4, 1022. Herbert de Vevre's and Elena Zimina's notes.

When we arrived at the Penelope, we discovered a qualitatively different level of interaction between the organisms of Eden. Unfortunately, on the Bare Ground we started observing the flora and fauna too late. We have our own theory about the unity of the flora and fauna of Eden, but we need to do independent research. It was decided that Herbert would take on the flora, and Elena the fauna. Each of us will write a report, and then we will try to bring our observations together.
r156113.n: Read the first page of the report on defense mutations

t: These are notes from the third report
r156114.n: These are notes from the third report

t: I am not setting foot in this pathetic wreck ever again. This would have never happened if harvesters were made on Umoir. Shame!
r156118.n: I am not setting foot in this pathetic wreck ever again. This would…

t:
Klavdia misled us, to put it mildly. "Here you will find the key to the victory over Nihaz," she said. "Find my Mother, she will be your ally," she said. We found no one! Even if we find her, there's no guarantee that she'll be any friendlier than the locals.

The only good thing here is ambrosia. This is the key to progress and development. I'm sure it will be the straw that will break Nihaz's back.

Since you're here, I need to keep you busy. There's the other base, Penelope. We've lost connection a while ago. We need to figure out why. As soon as we finish the ongoing things, you and I will go there.

Haven't I already told you that I do not wish to see you here? We were preparing for this expedition for a year. We calculated every step. Look at what you and Klavdia have done! Turned up here out of the blue! You were told to wait! Why couldn't you just be patient? Look around you. This world is completely different from others. We have no idea by what laws it is living. Of course, we had to get into trouble with these wild mud-diggers. How were we supposed to know that they'd hate us the moment they see us? I've never seen anyone so dim! Not even in the darkest corners of Umoir! I really don't think that you can do anything about them. Knowing your problem-solving skills, I assume the effect will be opposite.

Well, if that really is the case, then we won't be able to negotiate with the goddess either.

Sorry, but I'm not ready to give up the comforts of civilization to wrap myself in leaves and live on a tree.

We have no other choice. To save Sarnaut, we need the Ambrosia.
r156123.n: Hirkalla told me about that civilization - the ruins you had discovered. This is what…

t:
I suspected it might end like this.

We have nothing to offer them. Advanced magical technology? Holy icons? Gibberling beer? They don't need any of this.

They won't back down and compromise.

Well, if we can’t come to an agreement, then it's going to be easy.
r156124.n: The Children are not willing to give us the Ambrosia.

t: How is it going? Not very well, I see...

Great, I knew you could be counted on. Some natives from another world are less important than saving all of Sarnaut! I will try to let everyone in Sarnaut know about your feat.

Once everything is decided, remember that even if you change your mind, the Children are unlikely to welcome you back with open arms!
r156126.n: Yes. I will defend Sarnaut with the Expedition.

t:
It's a pity. I saw great potential in you, and you give up your future to protect some natives from another world. Everyone in Sarnaut will know about your decision!

And even if you change your mind, coming back will not be easy!
r156127.n: Yes. I will defend Eden together with the Children.

t:
Well, it's unfortunate, but I can understand your motives.

Is that right?

This is good news, but I want to make sure you don't falter at the crucial moment.

Is that right?
r156130.n: Expedition. I will do anything for my home world.

t:
Yes, you are the only one who hasn't decided yet. You need to make a choice.

If these Children and their goddess are so dear to you, you can go to them. I'm only letting you do this because I remember your past exploits. But the next time we meet, we'll be enemies. And if you are willing to defend our world, then I will be glad to see you in our ranks.

Whose side are you on? Decide! It's now or never!
r156131.n: So I have to make a choice...

t:
Is that so?

I always suspected that Zayan’s apprentices couldn't be trusted. While we needed Skulnar as a navigator on the Star Trail, the viper had no place here.

Fortunately, we can do without them now. The path is clear, the Gates can create a passage from Sarnaut to Eden without any help. And if we need to get into another world, we will find someone else for the job.

The only thing I don't understand is... Which side are you on?
r156132.n: Skulnar the Fierce and Eurial sympathize with the Children

t:
I knew it!

Zayan’s apprentices can't trusted, and neither can Klavdia. All these Orders of Creation and Balance are nothing but trouble. When Felix and I return to Sarnaut, we will deal with them all.

And Felix has already warned me that Skulnar the Fierce is very dangerous. Over time, he and his orcs will become a real threat to the Empire which is currently our ally. And as they say, the enemy of my enemy... is my enemy!

And Eurial is the daughter of Elleken, the Great Mage who has been wanted by the Conclave for crimes for over a millennium. She is his supporter and accomplice.

Fortunately, we can do without them now. The path is clear, the Gates can create a passage from Sarnaut to Eden without any help. And if we need to get into another world, we will find someone else for the job.

The only thing I don't understand is... Which side are you on?
r156133.n: Skulnar and Eurial have betrayed the Expedition!

t: Then you should do everything to win her over to our side. But as far as I remember, Skulnar the Fierce and Eurial went with you. For some reason I don't see them with you - where are they now?
r156134.n: Waterlily trusts me, so there is a chance.

t: This proves that the Children are fanatical. They believe in their goddess. Fortunately, we have experience in fighting gods and those who believe in them. However, I have a question. Skulnar the Fierce and Eurial were with you. Where are they now?
r156135.n: Waterlily is completely devoted to the All-Mother

t: That's how we wanted it to go when we sent you with Waterlily. But as you can see, you didn't get anywhere. Perhaps you managed to find allies among the Children who can act as an intermediary? What about this Waterlily?
r156136.n: I could persuade the All-Mother... Maybe

t: I already got that. Although when I sent you to negotiate with them, I thought we could find some common ground. As for Waterlily, she didn't seem to be as antagonistic. Perhaps it will be possible to establish communications through her?
r156137.n: The All-Mother is stubborn and proud. She will not give up her plans

t:
I don't see any room for compromise yet. We desperately need the Ambrosia, and the Children are zealously guarding their trees...

And if I understand the ideas of this All-Mother correctly, she does not want the worlds created by her to follow the path of technological development.
r156138.n: Do we have a chance to settle the matter peacefully?

t: You never learned to listen to me and obey, did you?
r156139.n: You never learned to listen to me and obey, did you?

t: Good. The Expedition will need your help. We are suffering heavy losses in this war, so every soldier counts.

I'm glad you couldn't forget us. The Expedition needs your help. But you won't be able to change your mind again any time soon.

Is the Hero of Sarnaut sure of their choice?

[Your reputation with the Children will be reset to Neutral!]
r156141.n: I'm glad you couldn't forget us. The Expedition needs your help. But…

t: You cannot change sides. You've chosen one just recently. You've sworn loyalty to the other party just recently.
r156142.n: I want to serve the Expedition again

t: There is a battle going on now,  We'll talk when it's over.
r156143.n: There is a battle going on now, We'll talk when it's over.

t: Now is not the time to switch sides. The war is in full swing and you need to complete your adventures on Eden before we can return to this discussion!
r156144.n: Now is not the time to switch sides. The war is in full swing and you…

t: I will not speak with a traitor to Sarnaut.
r156145.n: I will not speak with a traitor to Sarnaut.

t:
We didn't have enough engineers here to work with mana bombs - when I formed the Expedition, I recruited those who would build Ambrosia mining mechanisms, not weapons, you know...

However, it turns out that you did us a favor when you dragged that goblin Nogrom Junior here. He's supposedly a specialist in explosives.

And although I worry he'll blow up our base before he builds anything, I think it's worth giving him a chance under the circumstances.

Find out what exactly he needs to get it done.
r156146.n: What do we need to build it?

t:
Ambrosia Mana Bomb or A.M.B.Rosia Project? Well, it's an interesting idea.

I hear the Children told you about a world where people invented a weapon that splits the very essence of matter, causing monstrous damage.

"A.M.B. Rosia" will probably be something similar.

The principle here is simple: we close the energy circuits of an ordinary mana bomb to a concentrate in the crystal form, and the explosion starts a chain reaction with the gradual transformation of matter into energy.
r156147.n: Ask about creating a mana bomb

t: The Expedition is counting on you. We have a lot of problems in this world. The most important is the Ambrosia.
r156148.n: The Expedition is counting on you. We have a lot of problems in this…

t:
Still searching for the love of my life. Although it's just a tiny adventure for you, one of many, you might remember that we met before. On Gipat.

I was the dragon resistance leader, trying to disrupt the idiotic show. I'm sure you understand my motives better now. You know I was right!

Let me tell you one more secret. I was also one of Sarn's cultists. I hoped that he helps me find the love of my life.

There's no point in telling you the rest of the story. I haven't found what I've been looking for, and Sarn... well, you know.

But if the Spark isn't in Sarnaut, where can it be? I gave it a very good thought. Of course, there's the concept of "Heaven" in many religions, where all dead people go... But I had my doubts until I found out where all the Sparks go after leaving Sarnaut. You know where? To the world that can be safely called "Heaven."

Eden has been my destination ever since. Luckily, Klavdia sought our help. I took some of the cultists, the ones I knew well, and here we are.

Alas, our search is slow. Why? You will see... soon.

Ask me if you need teleportation or mailing services. We can set up steady connection with Sarnaut when you arrive.
Greetings in the new world! This is the true heaven.
r156155.n: Greetings in the new world! This is the true heaven.

t: Cheeky. But what choice have we got? That Great Mage caught us in a weak position. It's not that we had that much of a choice here. Keep an eye on him, he can pull some trick.

We were prepared to leave. I gathered everyone, found the right keys, prepared everything... and unleashed an avalanche!

The word about our journey quickly spread among those, who tried to capture the Star Gates in the Dead City. Namely, the Wormfaces from mountain caves, demons, cheated by Catherina, and Draconids... who cause the most problems.

Shortly before your arrival the power went out. The thing is, Draconids captured the local mana station and caused the outage.

I expect it to get even worse. Go now, or it will never happen. League and Imperial fleets are fighting a demonic onslaught near Suslanger but new demons keep arriving. From all Astral...

Here's what you need to do: enter the mana station and figure out why it stopped working. Besides, as Skulnar has been behind the Gates and seen what it's like, we need to get hazmat suits stat. No, assault shells won't work in these conditions. You can find equipment crates all over the camp. Unfortunately, most of the equipment didn't survive this mess. Try searching the boxes. We need half a dozen of suits. Backup won't hurt.
r156200.n: Ask what to do right now.

t:
Catherina was really reluctant to let you join the Expedition. Maybe she was superstitious, or maybe she believed in the Horizon prophecies too much. Remember what unthinkable disaster they promised after the demons set sail outside Sarnaut? You were supposed to perish after setting foot on their ship.

What a load of nonsense. We don't even have ships. Nevertheless, Catherina was strongly against demons and namely you in her Expedition. Well, I listened to her back then. This time, I'm going to do it my way.

I got you a dream team of your friends. Skulnar, Murk, Nogrom... and Eurial. Oh, quit staring. She's useful. Besides, Zayan really straightened her out. She's our loyal ally now, and she knows a lot about my Daddy's doings.

Your task is to follow Catherina's footsteps, find my mother's world, find out what happened to the Expedition, and persuade my mother to become Sarnaut's patron.

And... well... I must admit that I miss her. Tell her that as well.

Catherina didn't listen to me. She wanted her own Expedition. Of course, I could break up with her completely, hide Suslanger behind the veil of secret, and don't let anyone near the Gates... but I decided against it. Perhaps, that's what Nihaz wanted. I knew better.

I let them enter mother's world after infiltrating several loyal people in their Expedition. Sarn's former cultists, hehe. They really wanted to believe that my mother was capable of resurrecting their late god.

I was hoping that even if Catherina, Felix, and Ivan would fail, my people could at least deliver a note to my mother.

Something went wrong... Skulnar told me that after wandering along the Star Trail for a while they eventually managed to find the right world. They started building a base, and our unique friend returned together with a small group. Skulnar passed me Catherina's message: they'll be sending news every once in a while.

It's been several months now. There are no news. Whatsoever.

I need your help again.

I thought about her and decided to act. It was too easy to tip you off at Nihaz's Citadel. Cosmos played right into my hands, too. We gathered the army of the dead. Your next task was to distract Nihaz while I was dismantling the fortress to get the coordinates of my mother's world.

You see, she's been hiding out in her own world. She doesn't want to see anyone except her own creations. Nihaz had been looking for her world for years, and he might have found it in the end. He can't enter it but I'm sure his minions are already there.

I can't get in there either: I'm tied to Sarnaut and can't leave it. Moreover, the only Sarnaut's Star Gates have turned to stardust after the epic battle between Sarn and the Architect. I had to kick out both League and Empire and begin building my own Gates.

I've been on the lookout for Nihaz when this lady came by. Alice. She was messing with us. Thankfully, she decided to leave at some point. But as a result, this world got ambrosia, and Catherina and the others got the bit between the teeth. They wanted ambrosia more than anything in the world. And they got it into their heads that it was spilled from my mother's world.

So, I've got a plan how to fix everything. You see, Nihaz only looks scary. Everyone trusts his "Boo! I'm the evil God of Darkness! Fear me!" But in fact, he never risked facing an equal. All he's capable of is to pit his enemies against each other and then finish the survivor.

I was his loyal student. We made Sarn and the Architect annihilate one another. Nihaz is a whole different story. He's a harder nut to crack. He will never face us in a battle. But as they say in one of the worlds, the only weapon against a dragon is your own dragon.

We need our own divine patron. You might say that one would be just as bad as the other, or even worse... You're right. The gods you have had to face weren't very nice. But there is one god that will be happy to help us out.

My mother. Surprise-surprise, I also had a mom! In fact, despite the fact that I was Nihaz's step-daughter, I had a full set of real parents. I might have made my mother unhappy at some point, but since she's been at war with Nihaz longer than us, I'm sure we can find common ground.

All right, let's start from the beginning. To see what we want to achieve, you need to understand how it all started.

Six years ago we made Sarn and the Architect clash. It was an incredibly risky move but for the first time ever Sarnaut was free from cheeky and destructive gods. At least, that's how it seemed to me.

But Daddy did find a way to ruin our lives. Maverick made Kyros try to get rid of your Immortality. It's only natural that he lost but this wasn't the end.

I suspect that they needed all that for distraction. Nihaz's real target was the Well of Souls. He used it to return to Sarnaut, and I think he affected all newborn Aoidoi. Including Cosmos, who now plays his own games...

Then there was Sogot. Remember how the God of Darkness was trying to get into your head? Skulnar helped you fight it and break the connection. Back in the day, it caused me a great deal of effort to resist it.

What was next? Doomsday predictions? A journey beyond the horizon? You know, even I believed that it was inevitable. But now we have a chance to avoid such future.
r156205.n: What do you want to tell me?

t:
Catherina went off her rocker, apparently. Power drove her crazy. But that can be fixed - we already gave her a thrashing once.

What else do we have?

An ambitious imperial general? A greedy Free Trader?

Small fry.

I think you can easily deal with this whole rabble. So your task is to help the All-Mother get rid of especially impudent invaders, and then ask her to come to Sarnaut.

Ugh, I don't even know what to tell you...

Alright, let's stay calm...

NO! WHAT IN THE WORLD ARE YOU DOING?!

YOU HAD A SIMPLE TASK - TO FIND MY MOTHER AND SECURE HELP!!

WHAT IS CATHERINA DOING?

Go back to Eden immediately and order them to stop stealing the Ambrosia... from these... natives.

Yes, I understand that my mother can be difficult, but all you need to do is arrange for her to come here. I'll figure the rest out myself.
r156207.n: Tell them what you have managed to learn in Eden

t: Ah, here you are. I hope you realize that we couldn't do it without you.
r156210.n: Ah, here you are. I hope you realize that we couldn't do it without you.

t:
I couldn't have done this without you, "Hero of Sarnaut".

Want to know what's next?

A voice came from the Abyss.

"I don't recommend jumping into this chasm... The secrets it hides are beyond your understanding... And it will hurt when you fall. Leave. While you still can."

You ignored the strange voice and started descending. Strange cobwebs and unusual demons awaited you. The voice kept talking:

"So stubborn... What am I to do with you...?"

You kept going, through the cobwebs and the demons attacking you.

"You don't understand...  You resist... I've had enough of this!"

It's a strange place that seemingly spawns demons…

"This should stop you!"

As you descend into the Abyss, you run into a strange old man who looks more comical than threatening. The old man was waving a stick and shouting threats:

"Ah! You are forcing me to punish you. You will regret it! On the other hand... Who else would do it? No one, apparently... Well? Ready for your lesson? Let's begin!"

But the funny old man turned out to be extremely powerful. The fight was not easy. Those who had mind powers could hear the fragments of this Master's thoughts:

"You are making a mistake... Do not attempt to infiltrate my mind, fool! You will regret it!"

"I've been imprisoned for millions of years! I can wait a little longer."

"It gives me unbearable pleasure to destroy things I love most!"

"Nihaz... Nihaz... One day I will say this name for the last time!"

"I saw the creation and death of many worlds! You can never hope to challenge me, mortals!"

"Why? Why are you doing this? Go away, I don't want to hurt you. I have already done enough evil..."

"For thousands of years I've been a prisoner in a cage of my own fears... But now... When I have discovered how cunning my enemy is, nothing will stop me!"

"Please go. The innocents shall not suffer anymore. Your deaths will not save this world."

"No, I'm not broken! The years spent in prison tempered my rage! Run, insects, before my hatred burns you to ashes!"

"Well, well, well... You think you're heroes? You are flies caught in a web of delusion! And I will swat you!"

And when he was seemingly defeated, something incredible happened. The old man split into two parts: one was unthinkably beautiful, and the other was disgustingly terrible. A beautiful angel and a disgusting spider, so big that it filled the entire Abyss with its body.

"I will destroy you!" said the Dark Side.

"I will join in!" said the Light Side.

It was a terrible battle. Both the Light and Dark sides wielded immense power. By some miracle, you defeated them.

"Well, this is a victory... Your victory... But let's see what you say when the consequences follow! We will meet again, my children!" the creature said in the end.

Kazul the Astral Watcher. Gorluxor's Watchman. You crossed the quarters of the City of Demons and entered the Tower. Here, each step takes tremendous effort. Every step is a fallen cultist, demon, troll, or Searing Eye.

But the real challenge is still ahead. When he was still an Imperial Great Mage, Gorluxor experimented on living beings, trying to change them using special technology. Here, in the Tower he had rebuilt to his liking, he continued his experiments. The result is a powerful Searing Eye, a many-eyed watchman who does not let anyone get close to his master.

But it won't be an obstacle to you.
r156226.n: Tell me about Kazul the Astral Watcher

t:
Strina the Fierce The Lady of Death. Another one you've met before. Of course, only the Imperials know her true story. I'll tell you about it.

The Orcs do not have magic powers that would allow them to become Great Mages and hold their allod. It's a well-known fact. However, for many centuries, there has been a legend about an orc who had magic powers. The shamans did not know his name or where he came from and when he lived, but they started looking for his descendants.

More recently, they managed to get on the trail of these descendants. A family of two brothers and a sister was found. Stormrider, Skulnar, and Strina the Fierce However, when the shamans tried to win them over to their side, tragedies started befalling them. Stormrider was the first to die. Conscripted into the army, he fell during the League's attack on Igsh.

Strina was found next. The Hero of the Empire helped her avoid the problems associated with her gift, but then she refused to help the shamans and decided to choose her own fate after gaining a powerful ally.

Finally, Skulnar - his story is even more heartbreaking. He became a victim of the Empire's experiments. Transformed into a half-machine, he went mad during a diversion created by Tep and was killed during the cleanup of Lab-13.

Strina was found again on Coldberg where she tried to destroy the deposits of meteoric iron with her undead and demonic allies. After becoming a cultist, she became an enemy of this world and was also killed. As you can guess, Gorluxor was the ally she gained.

And now we meet her again. As you understand, death is not an obstacle for Gorluxor's allies, and Strina can ally herself even with Death. You have encountered Nogrom, one of her creations. And she is ready to summon more of those creatures.

The Orcs are not sorcerers, but Strina's gift made her strong enough to contend even with the Great Mages. She is a powerful summoner, which makes her extremely dangerous.

Armando de Doucer. A Vampire Knight, traitor to the Elves. The Patriarch of the House de Doucer.

You must have heard of him. But the people of the League know him best.

Let me remind you: he's a leader of one of the Great Elven Houses who violated the rules of the Great Game. During a Great Ball, he put a deadly curse on the bride of the man he lost to. When his actions were discovered, Armando and his House were exiled.

They dreamed of revenge, and Tep came to their aid. He granted Armando powers of astral darkness, and soon almost the entire House de Doucer turned into vampires. Armando once again intervened in the next Great Ball, capturing the Galleon Castle of the House de Ardeur and turning it into Darkblood Citadel. That's where justice was dispensed - by order of the Tenebran governor, Marguerite de Desirae, the heroes of the League cut off Armando's head.

You might remember that a severed head makes resurrection impossible. The spark cannot return to the body if it's missing the head. But as it turned out, Armando managed to get around it. You met him on Avilon, in another Galleon Castle which was created by Gorluxor this time. Armando boasted of his resurrection but was killed again.

And now you need to end his life again. For the last time. But the mystery of his resurrection remains unsolved for the time being.

Armando won't be alone - his inner circle will be with him. After leaving his wife Carmilla on Umoir, the Patriarch is ready to fight for Gorluxor and keep you from going any further. But it won't help him. You will win this time, too.
r156228.n: Armando de Doucer. A Vampire Knight, traitor to the Elves. The…

t:
Zalmar the Twisted. A demon leader. Don't think demons have gender. It's just a convention that has a symbolic meaning. War'kaz the Mindreaver was brutal, but Zalmar the Twisted is insidious. A skilled mage who channels the power of the Astral, she has killed many.

In the City of Demons, she is tasked with collecting and protecting the mana Gorluxor and his henchmen may need.

Of course, your task was to eliminate her. If you were able to get past her, you could keep going.
r156229.n: Tell me about Zalmar the Twisted

t:
War'kaz the Mindreaver A demon commander. He can do everything they can. But better. This demon is focused destruction. Someday you will understand the true meaning of my words, but for now...

The thing is, demons don't have names. Just the nicknames you or the cultists give them. Few can remember this demon. Because few survived an encounter with him. I could tell you about the ships he sank, the allods he burned down.

This astral demon lived in the most fiery sectors of the astral. Now he is called here to protect this city.

Of course, he is extremely dangerous. And, of course, you defeated him.

Excellent. So you decided to go in. But surely you didn't expect it to be easy? It wasn't. The City of Demons is divided into quarters cleverly connected by demonic portals. With the help of your Great Mages, Aidenus and Yasker, you learned how to hack them. You move forward, stepping over the bodies of those madmen who crave the destruction of the world. Who leads them? You can only guess.

As you already know, this demonic cult is an example of a complex hierarchy. But even a cult needs those who will just stand guard. At the start, it is Gog and Magog, two trolls clad in armor. After slaying them, you stop in front of a cup of blood. Use the blood of the cultist you killed and draw the attention of the real threat - the dead ogre Nogrom.

Demons and necromancy? We will talk about this later. The ogre is powerful, and the blows of its club will knock you down. But he is nothing to the heroes of Sarnaut. Victory lets you decide where to go next. Old enemies or new ones?

Aidenus found out about it and said:

"I see... Not the news I thought I'd hear. Now listen to me. After the catastrophe, people needed a symbol to unite around, and that's what we gave them. Well, twelve symbols. The dead can no longer be saved, but their memories remain with the living. And the power... Does it matter who has it if they use it for good? Power is neutral. But people, sentient beings, are polarized. To be honest, it's nice to have my suspicions confirmed. For now, it's not important which ones. As for the Star Gates, I'm actually pleased to know that they are inaccessible to us.  Imagine what would have happened if we had gotten our hands on them. The Gibberlings would have found themselves a new land. The great Elven houses would have sprung up everywhere, then quickly withered due to lack of challenge and competition. As for the Kanians, they would've lost their roots, forgotten their ancestors and their faith... And what is a people without roots? Dust on the roads of history! It will be better if you don't tell everyone what you've learned..."

Apparently Yasker said the same thing:

"Hmm... I wasn't wrong. This is not good news. But it looks like you did the right thing. The Star Gates... Can you imagine what would have happened if the Empire had taken them? We would have probably succumbed to temptation and set off to conquer new worlds. The Empire would have grown too big and gained too much power. And then? I'm tempted by these lovely visions, but I know what unfettered expansion brings. Believe me, I've seen it, and it's tragic. Now, about the Patrons. And don't tell anyone what you know. Yes. There were no great martyrs. But this is one of the biggest state secrets, one of many that you need to keep to yourself. People needed a symbol to unite around, and that's what we gave them. Well, twelve symbols. The dead can no longer be saved, but their memories remain with the living. You can tell the Keeper of Secrets everything you know, but no one else should know this!"

The Star Gates are still in the Dead City. Now inaccessible, they were useless. Perhaps eventually someone would find a Key that would open them. But it's a completely different story.
r156233.n: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in the Dead City

t:
It's been a long time since you walked along the path that the God of Darkness suggested. You became his faithful disciples and followers, even though he did not demand worship from you. Here in the Dead City, you have recognized his lies and found the courage to challenge him.

Nihaz was probably surprised. This battle was legendary, but you won.

"Ungrateful scum! ME! I uplifted you! I gave you powers! I gave you knowledge that exists nowhere else in the universe! And this is how you repay me? You should have heeded the old saying about the hand that feeds you! Traitor... I hoped that at least someone in this universe was able to appreciate the beauty of my ideas. I gave you a better life... And this is how you repay me?! That winged worm put you up to this? To betray your daddy? Not good...

You really think that ordinary weapons can kill a god? Hahaha! You were able to destroy my physical body, this husk. Too bad my little girl isn't around... But that’s fine. Presently I might not be in the condition to turn you to ash on the spot, but remember, vermin: I will return. And if I happen to be in a good mood, I'll give you one more chance to serve me. You'd better agree when that happens, or else the tortures that my friend Sarn endured will pale in comparison!

Remember, fool: only the gods or forces equal to gods can destroy gods. And you, parasites, are abusing this power! Patrons... what a joke. It's nothing but another lie. Even your lies are pathetic... There are no Patrons. Or rather, all your mages died in the Cataclysm. They are dead. And the Surges you and your allies use so brazenly - I created them! First I gave some of my power to the dragons, but those brainless lizards wasted it. The power spilled out of them like water from a torn waterskin. Predictably, they were left weak and vulnerable... The Junes took advantage of it, mowing them down. Then I replaced the useless dragons with the Seals: concentrated power that would keep Sarn imprisoned.

If it hadn't been for your Cataclysm, the whole thing might have lasted for quite a while. Luckily for Sarn and unluckily for us, the catastrophe affected the Seals, and part of their power was lost to the Astral. Part of my power! The power of the dragons, the remnants of which were used by your mages, and the power of the Seals, which you believe is the power of your Patrons - all this power came from me! Do you really think you can destroy me with my own weapons?

Frankly, I'm not even offended by your actions. Furthermore, I would have questioned your bravery and ambition if you hadn't challenged me. But I must say you picked the wrong time to interfere. You still can't use the Gates, no matter how hard you try. As for you, we'll meet again!"

And then the Dark God vanished... You need to inform the leaders of the states.

When traveling through the Misty Lands, you probably noticed that they are full of the brainless undead. But where do they come from?

Let me tell you: the Dead City wasn't always dead. The Black Night destroyed it - you also know it as the Cataclysm. One monarch once ruled over this land...

Nihaz will tell you the rest:

"Here in the throne room of the Dead City, I sense the presence of something I can't see...

It's a ghost! The last ruler of the Dead City, as far as I can tell. What does he want?

Oh, so that's it! He was not slain in a fair fight, as befits a king, but fell at the hand of a hired killer. A familiar story... Now he wants another, peaceful death. For this to happen, he requests that we remove the relics that belonged to him in life. We will then resurrect him for a short time and slay him in a proper fight.

Shall we help this long-dead king, or should we leave him to haunt the ruins?"

Of course you decided to help. Although that king had no intention of dying peacefully...

"Aha! Prepare for battle! Something tells me that the ghost wants to go to eternal rest, surrounded by fallen enemies, as befits a true leader!

Can you hear those hushed whispers in the corners of the hall? Those are the ghosts of the Dead City. They have come to pay a tribute of respect to their lord! I don't know if he was a good king or a bad one, but he will die a royal death, he he! To fall by the hand of the great heroes of Sarnaut is an honorable end. What's more, you can expect a truly royal reward, so prepare for battle.  It will be a difficult fight!"

Thanks to you, the king can rest in peace. Your reward is waiting for you...

"The Dead King can finally rest in peace.  The ancient tragedy has come to its proper conclusion. And you receive the armor of the dead king as the winner."
r156235.n: Tell me about the Dead King

t:
Have you dealt with the Earth Destroyer? Excellent. I appreciate that. Let my godling friend sit in limbo and think about what he's done, right? Haha!"

Those were the words of the Dark God. But there was also news from the former God of Light...

"As soon as you approach the slowly dissolving shape of the defeated demon, your mind is flooded with visions.

You see Sarn struggling against the darkness that binds his body, radiating pure white light. Every motion causes him to flinch in pain, and his body remains stained by the shadow of darkness. The stains grow with each attempt to escape.

You can see that Nihaz is playing a game with the imprisoned god, a cruel experiment where every attempt at freeing himself brings Sarn closer to his breaking point where he will have no strength left to battle darkness, becoming just like Nihaz. The god of darkness has entertained himself for years, offering Sarn the chance to escape from his prison, but then dashing his hopes at the last moment.

You see a strange structure installed in the throne room of the Dead City, and you can see that it's the Star Gates, Sarn's last hope. If the demons could take the gates, then Sarn would be freed. He could leave this world. But Nihaz once again uses others to fight battles for him - the heroes of this universe who believed in his good intentions.

History repeats itself... Once, the Junes believed Nihaz, and it destroyed them. The same fate awaits both the League and the Empire. The only chance to escape the tragic lot of the Junes is to stop Nihaz before it's too late."

Sarn's attempt to escape from his prison. I think I'll let Nihaz speak this time. He is the Director, after all:

"Well then, it's time to deal with Sarn's demons. Our prisoner's starting to get a little restless. Who knows, he might actually be able to break out of his prison. If that happens, I won't be able to rebuild it; I'll just have to smite him. But he's more useful to me in one piece. It's fascinating how with every attempt to free himself, he acquires a new dark stain on his offensively pure soul. He'll never get those stains out, haha...

Here in the Dead City, demons obey the Earth Destroyer - a self-propelled battering ram capable of "destroying the walls of a jail cell" and freeing its creator. Jokes aside, this time Sarn created almost a perfect executor of his plans, a helper who brings only death and destruction. More and more, Sarn reminds me of myself when I was young! I was always trying to create all kinds of different monsters before I learned that brute force always loses to careful calculation.

But brute force might just do the trick in this situation. So, my friend, I need you to hunt down the Earth Destroyer. It's a powerful foe, but if you can put together a good team, you'll defeat it without any trouble."

I should add that Sarn's demons were already on the surface of allods by that time, far from the astral plane. These are not Kirah creatures that died like fish out of water. The Earth Destroyer did not need the Astral - he carried the Astral to you. It's a machine for processing material into primary matter. I'm really glad you managed to bring it down.
r156237.n: Tell me about the Earth Destroyer

t:
You may have heard this from me before, but demons don't have proper names. They don't even know the meaning of having one. However, the cultists of Sarn, who have ordinary inhabitants of Sarnaut in their ranks, have given them names.

There is an ancient Kanian legend about the mysterious Nav's Kingdom which is the exact opposite of the real world. And its mistress Nav lives there.

We will not be analyzing the eschatology of primitive tribes and wonder if there is something real behind this. Another important thing is that one of Sarn's creatures was named Nav. Why? Well, it's a demon of such psionic power that it can distort reality... Create a copy of reality. And the rules of that reality are established by Nav!

This... Nav is dangerous, smart and even seductive in a way. Her charms will make you fall into her arms. Things look bad, but then a third party intervenes - this time the Wormfaces. They hate Sarn's Curse which destroyed their people. They distracted Nav, wore her out, and you and other heroes finished what they started.

So, the Great Dragon... It's ironic that we meet him here... after all, it was here that he once met Ath-Zak. This date went much more peacefully back then. But the Fiery Father's current goals made him reckless.

I must say there is a lot of confusion when it comes to dragons. There are too few of them, so any dragon that is slightly bigger than a horse is called Great. But no, the real Great Dragons are also the Keepers. It's the dozen that guarded Sarn at the dawn of the world. And their descendants like Soliskar the Wise and Agrus the Callous are just... teenagers. They have yet to become Great. If, of course, they are allowed to. Doesn't it surprise you that they aren't here?

But let us get back to the Fiery Father. Oh, he's careful. Otherwise, he wouldn't have survived the massacre carried out by the Junes. But now he's so close to his goal, and it makes him vulnerable. I will quote our immortal classic:

"You know what I hate more than anything? Stupid, petty betrayal.

Take the Great Dragon, for example. I forgave him for failing to defend the prison. Everyone makes mistakes. But his attempt to wage war against me is like a pup trying to pick a fight with a big wolfhound - pointless and stupid. It seems he has forgotten who he's dealing with! I'll have to remind him.

Go with the troop to the Upper City and rid me of this overgrown lizard. He's no longer useful to me."
r156241.n: So, the Great Dragon... It's ironic that we meet him here... after…

t:
You must be interested in Nihaz's Seals and the Keys to them. But this is not the time for that. It's enough that you know they exist and that they are extremely important. Not everyone can handle their power. I'll give you a hint: any of your Great Mages can do it.

But as you understand, the Draconids do not have Great Mages. None of them would drink dragon blood. However, to achieve his goal in the Dead City, the Fiery Father needed someone who could handle the Seals. That someone was Lickflame Tinderbox, the Great Draconid Shaman.

Of course, demons hated him. Still, he's one of the first children of the Fiery Father, the one who could ruin Sarn's plans. That's what doomed Lickflame. And he had no chance of surviving an encounter with you.

Sad, isn't it? But as Nihaz said, what's the point of a Play without a tragedy? Good authors kill off their characters often.

Our world is an amazing place. Sarn was a very inspired creator. Even when building the perfect destroyers of his prison, he created a great variety of creatures...

There is some sad irony in the fact that many of them joined his jailers. I'm talking about dragons and those who serve them. Do you know that the drakes were created by Sarn for the purpose of opposing the winged guardians? But here's another cause for sarcasm - only black drakes, considered by all to be traitors, serve their true creator.

But let's get to the point. At a time when the world was intact, among the creatures that inhabited it were terrestrial dragon-like creatures - salamanders, huge fire-breathing lizards. Now there are very few of them left, but you were going to meet one that has survived to this day. Thunderhead, the Gate Keeper. The "faithful dog" of the Draconids and the Fiery Father, placed here to keep you from going any further.

Do I need to say who came out the winner?

"So Zak is still as chatty as ever?

Right, so I won't have to listen to his babbling for the next few centuries. Ha ha!

Perhaps I'll even move his Spark to a new body after a while... After all, his people almost defeated the dragons, and he alone had enough pride and courage to stand against me. Which means there's still hope for him."

That's the epitaph the last of the Junes got from the Dark God. But he told you something...

"Finally... You have no idea how much I've suffered in this body! Cursed Nihaz... It's all his fault. His lies led my people to a disgraceful end.

You are but a blind pawn in the dark god's game. I'm thankful that you've put an end to my suffering. I'll tell you the real reason that compelled me to challenge Nihaz.

Long ago, when my people were strong, we nearly wiped out the dragons. But then Nihaz appeared and said that if Sarn were to be freed, the universe would be destroyed, along with all of us. Nihaz can be convincing. He showed us the Star Gates, a structure that the gods use to travel between worlds. He promised he would give us a new world where we would reign. When Sarn cursed my people, the survivors ran to Nihaz, begging him to fulfill his promise.

What's interesting is that Nihaz almost never tells a downright lie. And he wasn't lying then, either. We were given a new world. A world of damp, subterranean caves and eternal darkness. The curse stopped following those who were no longer Junes.

Nihaz speaks the truth, but his words are pure poison, for the truth is different for everyone. And you always hear the truth that you want to hear. It's not too late to come to your senses! Challenge Nihaz and take him down. Otherwise, sooner or later his lies will destroy you more surely than the sharpest blade!"

I will have repeat other people's words again. As you understand, after your meeting with Ath-Zak in Tka-Rik's Cave, he was resurrected. The Wormfaces used the same plans that you were going to use to give Osip a new body. Someone else's body...

I'll warn you just in case: without a properly hardened Spark, it's a disastrous idea. The spark is attached to the body. Trying to shove it into another is like trying to wear clothes that don't fit. It is very, very difficult to comprehend the possibility of rebirth... Ath-Zak was not ready for this.

But I will quote Nihaz and repeat the orders he gave you:

"It's time to end one of the plotlines in our play. Zak is a pain in the neck, frankly speaking. Capricious and ignorant. And yet you all consider him to be some sort of hero? So he defeated a demon, but only just, and he did that with the help of a Great Mage. Pshaw!

Either way, the fools that snatched his Spark consider him something of a deity. They follow him like sheep. Once was not enough for them, apparently. We'll have to teach them another lesson.

Pass through the gates to the Lower City and deal with Zak once and for all. As a Spark he's much more tolerable.

Of course, it wasn't easy to defeat the last of the Junes. But is there anything you can't do?

I have a suspicion that of all the enemies of Nihaz, you have the least sympathy for demons. But the Wormfaces are a different matter. Which is unsurprising: you had a chance to meet them back on Gipat, and Ath-Zak's story inspires certain sympathy for this hero.

I will share with you one secret policy of our close friends: while they call themselves the Overmind and maintain constant psionic contact, there are many individualists among them. The Wormfaces are not as united as they appear to be.

And you were about to meet with the leaders of this campaign: Shilonen, Coatl, and Atslan. The Wormface mentors.

One of them was once a great sage and philosopher, the second was a powerful mage, and the third was a most skilled warrior. But their skills did not help them in the fight against Sarn's curse, and then they crawled on their knees to Nihaz and became what they are today. Their long life is also the result of Nihaz's gift. Or another curse? Depends on how you look at it...

Even back then, this trio was spinning a web of intrigues, unaware that the Great Dragon also wanted them dead. Nihaz pitted his enemies against each other, and you helped finish them off.
r156246.n: Tell me about the Warmface Mentors

t:
During their heyday, the Junes were extremely powerful. Thanks to their considerable talents, they were able to create autonomous mechanisms - golems. This mixture of magic and technology may seem crude to you now, but believe me - even now you have nothing on what the Junes could do.

Golems did all the dirty and hard work for them. In many ways, it was thanks to them that their empire was able to defeat the dragons, because the numerous caves that the Wormfaces now inhabit are shelters of ancient times, dug out by golems for protection against the fire-breathing creatures.

Of course, the Junes also tried to create battle golems. You already know Ram Shaitan, the guardian of the Frontier, but the golems created shortly before the fall were perfect machines of destruction. Ultranis is one of their prototypes, and its power is shocking.

However, as you already know, the golems did not save the Junes from the Curse. Ultranis is strong but not invulnerable. That's why you were able to defeat it.

"Right behind me you can see the entrance to the second stage, lit by the crimson flame of the scaly horde of the Draconids and their Fiery Father. They tried to outplay me on my own turf. And they failed. They just don't know it yet, haha.

Finally, behind the third set of gates are the once-great Junes who now resemble a drunkard's nightmare: the Wormfaces led by their relentless leader, Zak. It was his Spark they were able to steal from me on the Isle of Revelation. He has a new body now... But something tells me he's not happy with it.

The best part is that all of them - the Draconids, the Wormfaces, and Sarn's demons - all fear something more than they fear me! They are afraid that someone else will get here first, to the heart of the Dead City. Each of them is trying to reach an agreement with me behind the others' backs, promising to help destroy what they imagine are my enemies. Hah! Just think about it: they all want to settle their scores with their long-time enemies by having someone else do the dirty work!

You can probably guess what brought the Wormfaces, the Draconids, and even the demons here, to the Dead City? Hehe. Look up! See that huge structure? That is the key... and lock in one. But let's leave its purpose a secret for now. You will learn everything in due time. One shouldn't change horses in midstream, right?

Let the play begin!"

So, each of the three enemies of Nihaz dreamed of a prize, something that's in the very center of the Dead City. At first, you didn't understand what exactly you were seeing… Understanding will come later. And now you had to choose which of the enemies of the Dark God will be defeated first.

You want to know about your possible future?

Well, surprises await you... But let's start from the beginning. You have joined the Game of the Gods that Dadd... Nihaz and Sarn started. You already know some of the details of their confrontation. But new pieces appeared on this board - the Great Dragon, aka the Fiery Father, and Ath-Zak, the June hero, and they all made their moves.

I'll give the floor to Nihaz:

"Welcome to the Dead City, my trusty helper! Are you still trying to understand the secrets of the world? That's quite commendable! I've already told you that brawn alone won't get you far. It's not enough to be physically strong. You have to know how to apply this strength. And this is why you're here now. The throne room of the Dead City is where everything started, and it's where everything will end... All the figures in our story are already in their places, eager to play their roles in our new play. Three acts on three stages! And you will be playing the lead role. For my part, I'll stay here in the audience.

Look right. Behind this gate is the first stage - the ruins defiled by demons. I'm sure they're just dying to break free and tear everyone in the audience to shreds. It's too bad they're too weak to tussle with a god. No matter what they do, their powers are essentially useless, because the gates open on my command!"
r156249.n: Yes, I want to know what happens in the Dead City..

t:
"I think you have already guessed the bitter truth, so I'm just going to dispel all remaining doubts. The Grand Experiment and the Cataclysm are one and the same!

Blinded by our pride, we searched for ways to increase our power. We found the Sources. We had no idea what the Seals were and why they were important. Every one of the Great Mages wanted only one thing - power, free power! We tried to master the power of the Seals. When our first attempt failed, we continued to attack the Source Seal again and again with the most powerful spells until it cracked and released its power into the world. Power against power, you know? The Seals gave way, the world's shell cracked, and the Astral put an end to the Sarnaut as I knew it. You know the rest - the world in ruins, the legend of the Patrons, the Great Mages being the last stronghold of order in a realm of chaos... But I see that you don't believe my words.

I may be dead, but I cherish hope that my death at least partly made up for the great debt of all the Great Mages since the Cataclysm!

I don't expect you to believe me. I wouldn't believe me either. But I have proof.

I recorded the Grand Experiment in detail for future generations, but I never had the courage to reveal the truth. I know that's cowardice, but the truth would mean the end of our world as we know it. A few mages were killed by mad commoners in the first years after the Cataclysm. Then the rebels died themselves, so there was no one left to protect their allods from the Astral. Just imagine what would've happened if I'd announced that it'd been us, the Great Mages, who destroyed this world? No, I could never do that. Yet the truth... The truth had to be preserved.

There is a cache in the tower in the center of Novograd. There's a column in a hall on the second story, the floor dented at its foundation. Utter the words I'll tell you next to that column, and the cache will open. Use the papers inside as you deem appropriate, but remember that the truth can kill faster than the sharpest sword!"

The heroes took the papers to Lovewise Catfish. He was shocked:

"What? What's in these papers? Let me see...

I can't believe my eyes! Those mages caused the Cataclysm and almost destroyed the whole world? I don't believe it! I don't want to believe it! But the journal...

You know, here's what I think. It doesn't matter what happened. The Great Mages paid for their mistake already by becoming prisoners of their own allods.  It's not for you or me to judge them.

I'll keep these papers, put them on the top shelf, and do my best to forget all about them. The people believe in the wisdom and power of the Great Mages, and that faith supports them better than any true knowledge. Sometimes it's better not to know. It's enough to simply believe."

So you still had questions: who helped Tep gain divine power? Where did Klavdia go and why?
r156250.n: Ask what Skrakan said about the Grand Experiment

t:
You haven't had enough? Shouldn't we stop here? Oh, well.

Before the heroes could recover from the shock after Klavdia's disappearance, the ghosts of Skrakan and Nezeb appeared before them! They had been imprisoned in Tep's Pyramid all this time...

You only had to question them...

This is what Skrakan said:

 "Light... Sounds... Life... I haven't felt all this in such a long time!

Don't be afraid of me. I'm a captive of Tep's, like the other prisoners of this pyramid. I spent a few years bound by a powerful spell once, yet that was nothing compared to the absolute power this mad warlock has over defenseless Sparks!

Allow me not to say my name. It's tarnished forever! What we thought of as a great triumph proved a great disaster. I did not learn from my mistake, and the blood of innocents was spilled again because of me... The Great Astral Campaign... The Great Bloody Campaign... No, don't ask me anything! Those are deeds of a distant past, and I've had enough time to realize the depth of my disgrace. And my tormentor Tep contributed greatly to that. When he got a new body, he often tormented my incorporeal spirit with tales of his great triumph that our mistake made possible.

You already know a lot about the Seals that we knew as the Sources. A lot, but not everything!

It will be a while before I feel brave enough to face the descendants of those who perished because of me. You will be the one to tell them this. Use my knowledge as you deem appropriate, but don't make our mistake again. Don't let your pride cloud your mind!

Tep... I'm still amazed at the power in his madness. Who would have thought that one day the once-dead man would try to drag the whole world into oblivion?

It scares me how easily Tep dealt with his enemies. How easily he created a whole world, albeit an illusory one. If it's not divine power, then it's something very close to one. And I think I know what the secret of his incredible power is. It's the Seals!

I know that Tep experimented with a small fragment of one of the Seals and drew power from it to create his Plague. This is one of the manifestations of the Sources - the manifestation of death. But the Pyramid… Illusions, energy, matter, the creation of new life and the impact on the mind. A full set of powers available to the Great Mages, and on top of that, the most elaborate curses. No, I don't believe that Tep could achieve all this alone. Until recently, he was just a body howling in pain, stuck between life and death. I'm sure Tep had help! And it was someone who knows everything about our Great Experiment."
r156251.n: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in Tep's Pyramid
